search_log: Searched “Erich Segal Love Story excerpt first chapter Oliver narrator,” title/author plus point of view and first-person terms, and library/Google Books preview variants.

Opened the Hodder/LoveReading exclusive opening, ReadingGroupGuides chapter-one excerpt, the official Erich Segal page, the Washington Post review, and the Adam Mickiewicz University Press scholarly article.
Searched specifically for epistolary form, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; no evidence of another sustained narrative person was found.
Open Library supplied edition metadata and a preview-only notice but no usable prose in the opened page.

The opened BookRags study-guide page called the novel third person while simultaneously assigning narration and voice to Oliver; this internally inconsistent, unattributed claim was rejected against the primary first-person prose and scholarly whole-book analysis.
person_note: The quote sample repeatedly exposes Oliver Barrett IV as a participating I-narrator, including event prose and narratorial beats embedded around dialogue. The Hodder opening independently confirms that several dialogue-bucket items contain first-person base narration; q01714 is a clear upstream bucket issue. Pure character speech and the generic-you gnomic question were not allowed to vote. A Tier B whole-book analysis identifies the novel as Oliver’s first-person memoir, resolving the opening excerpt’s limited scope. No sustained second- or third-person strand, epistolary structure, or alternating narrator was found; remaining uncertainty is minimal.
